mechanism_fit: M17 (type-semantic, index vs count). The field ParserBase._tokenInputCol can hold either a 0-based column index or a 1-based column number. The variant's ReaderBasedJsonParser.nextToken stores _inputPtr - _currInputRowStart. Because _inputPtr has already moved past the token's first character, that value counts the row's characters up to and including it, which is the 1-based column. The field should hold the 0-based index. The shared consumer ParserBase.getTokenColumnNr then adds its documented +1, so every reader-parser token column comes out one too high. Locally, either side could be the culprit: the producer storing a count, or the consumer converting twice. The correct reading is fixed elsewhere in the repository: (1) the field javadoc in ParserBase ('0-based (although in the end it'll be converted to 1-based)'); (2) JsonLocation.getColumnNr, documented as 1-based; (3) the byte-stream parser doing the same step with '- 1' (UTF8StreamJsonParser.nextToken and nextFieldName); (4) the passing test TestJsonParser.testKeywords, which asserts column 1 for the first token through the shared getTokenColumnNr. The failure signature 'expected:<1> but was:<2>' fits the gold, getTokenColumnNr, getTokenLocation and the row-start helpers alike.
gold: com.fasterxml.jackson.core.json.ReaderBasedJsonParser::nextToken (src/main/java/com/fasterxml/jackson/core/json/ReaderBasedJsonParser.java). Edit: '_tokenInputCol = _inputPtr - _currInputRowStart - 1;' becomes '_tokenInputCol = _inputPtr - _currInputRowStart;'. Restoring '- 1' is the minimal repair.

ownership_reason: ReaderBasedJsonParser.nextToken owns the fault. The field it writes, ParserBase._tokenInputCol, is documented in ParserBase as 0-based and converted to 1-based later. That conversion happens once, for every parser, in ParserBase.getTokenColumnNr (col + 1), and JsonLocation.getColumnNr documents its value as 1-based. When nextToken records the token start, _skipWSOrEnd has already consumed the token's first character. So _inputPtr - _currInputRowStart is the 1-based column, not the 0-based index the field holds. The variant stores that count and getTokenColumnNr adds +1 on top: the first '[' reports column 2, and 'true' on line 2 reports 4. The repository fixes the convention in several places: UTF8StreamJsonParser.nextToken and nextFieldName(SerializableString) use '_tokenInputCol = _inputPtr - _currInputRowStart - 1;'; the char-offset assignment two lines above the gold line also subtracts 1; and ParserBase.getCurrentLocation converts the next-character index with '+ 1 // 1-based'. The competitors are correct and pinned. getTokenColumnNr and getTokenLocation are shared with UTF8StreamJsonParser, and the passing test TestJsonParser.testKeywords asserts column 1 for that parser's first token, so dropping the +1 or subtracting 1 in getTokenLocation breaks it (checked: testKeywords fails). The loadMore rebasing and the _skipLF row start each shift only one line of the trigger (line 1 or line 2), so neither can make all the column assertions pass. Restoring '- 1' in nextToken alone makes the trigger pass with the full suite green.
trigger: com.fasterxml.jackson.core.json.TestJsonParser::testTokenColumnsAcrossLines (JUnit3, added to src/test/java/com/fasterxml/jackson/core/json/TestJsonParser.java). It parses "[ [\n  true ] ]" with the reader-based parser and keeps getTokenLocation() for the outer '[', the inner '[' and 'true'. It reads to the end of input before asserting anything. Then it asserts line/column 1:1, 1:3 and 2:3. Recording first means the line-feed path (_skipLF) runs before the first failing assertion, and the trigger checks columns on both line 1 and line 2.

concerns:
1. Probably easy to solve. There are strong local and nearby cues: the char-offset line two lines above the gold subtracts 1; UTF8StreamJsonParser has the identical line with '- 1'; getTokenColumnNr carries the comment 'convert from 0-based to 1-based'; and the field javadoc states the convention. I did not remove any of this. Expect a NULL screening class unless the model misreads the double conversion.
2. The test calls the gold method directly (jp.nextToken()). It is a large method (about 150 lines) and the fault is one line in it.
3. A quirk that was already in this Jackson version: JsonReadContext.getStartLocation passes the stored 0-based column straight into JsonLocation, so error-message start locations are 0-based. It is not on the trigger path, but a model could cite it as support for storing a 1-based column. The field javadoc, testKeywords and the UTF-8 parser still decide ownership.
4. Another existing quirk: in this version, the token location of a value that follows a comma or a field name points at the comma or field name. The trigger avoids commas and objects so that its expected values match the pristine behaviour.
5. Columns are barely covered by the existing tests, which is why the fault survives the suite. An odd edit to some other line (for example a different loadMore rebasing) could in principle hide line-1 columns, but the two-line trigger defeats the natural single-site row-start edits.
